# `silk/crypto/hmac`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Compute HMAC tags (RFC 2104) with SHA-256 or SHA-384.

## When to use
Use [`HmacSha256`](#HmacSha256) or [`HmacSha384`](#HmacSha384) to prove that a message comes from someone who has a shared
secret key and was not changed, for example to sign a webhook or a cookie. Use `silk.crypto.hkdf` to
derive keys, and `silk.crypto.sha2` for a hash without a key.

## Details
[`HmacSha256.authenticate`](#HmacSha256.impl.authenticate) returns the tag of one message. For a message that arrives in parts,
call `make` with the key, then `update` for each part, then `finish`. Any key length is valid. A
key longer than the block size (64 bytes for SHA-256, 128 for SHA-384) is hashed first. Nothing
allocates.

## Gotchas
This module computes tags, but it does not compare them. To check a received tag, compare all
bytes in constant time, as the example shows. Do not use `==` or a loop that stops at the first
difference. The states hold key material and are not erased when they are dropped.

## Examples
### Check a received tag
```silk
import silk.crypto.hmac { HmacSha256 }
import silk.num.u8

// Compares in constant time, so the time does not tell an attacker how many bytes match.
fn same(left: &[u8; 32], right: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {
  let mut difference: u8 = 0
  let mut index: usize = 0
  while index < 32 {
    difference = u8.bitOr(difference, u8.bitXor(left[index], right[index]))
    index = index + 1
  }
  return difference == 0
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let key = b"key"
  let message = b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
  let received = HmacSha256.authenticate(key, message)
  let mut state = HmacSha256.make(key)
  state.update(b"The quick brown fox ")
  state.update(b"jumps over the lazy dog")
  let expected = state.finish()

  // HMAC-SHA-256 of this key and message is f7bc83f4...d8.
  if !same(&received, &expected) || expected[0] != 0xf7 || expected[31] != 0xd8 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

## `HmacSha256`

```silk
pub struct HmacSha256
```

A streaming HMAC-SHA-256 state (RFC 2104) that returns a 32-byte tag.

Call [`HmacSha256.make`](#HmacSha256.impl.make) with the key, [`HmacSha256.update`](#HmacSha256.impl.update) for each part of the message, then
[`HmacSha256.finish`](#HmacSha256.impl.finish). For one message, use [`HmacSha256.authenticate`](#HmacSha256.impl.authenticate). The state is a
fixed-size value. It holds key material and is not erased when it is dropped.

### When to use

Use it to prove that a message comes from someone who has a shared secret key and was not
changed, for example to sign a webhook or a cookie. Use `silk.crypto.hkdf` to derive keys, and
`silk.crypto.sha2` for a hash without a key.

### Details

Any key length is valid. A key longer than the block size (64 bytes) is hashed first. Nothing
allocates.

### Gotchas

It computes tags, but it does not compare them. To check a received tag, compare all bytes in
constant time. Do not use `==` or a loop that stops at the first difference.

<a id="HmacSha256.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub fn make(key: &[u8]) -> HmacSha256
```

Returns an HMAC-SHA-256 state for `key`. Any key length is valid, also 0.

A key longer than 64 bytes is hashed first. The state copies what it needs and does not borrow
`key`.

<a id="HmacSha256.impl.update"></a>

### Method `update`

```silk
pub fn update(self: &mut Self, bytes: &[u8]) -> ()
```

Adds `bytes` to the end of the message.

Any split of the message into parts gives the same tag. An empty slice changes nothing.

#### Gotchas
The program traps if the message is longer than 2^64 - 1 bits minus the 64-byte key block.

<a id="HmacSha256.impl.finish"></a>

### Method `finish`

```silk
pub fn finish(self: Self) -> [u8; 32]
```

Returns the 32-byte HMAC-SHA-256 tag of the message and consumes the state.

<a id="HmacSha256.impl.authenticate"></a>

### Associated function `authenticate`

```silk
pub fn authenticate(key: &[u8], message: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32]
```

Returns the 32-byte HMAC-SHA-256 tag of `message` with `key`.

An empty key or message is valid. To check a received tag, compare all bytes in constant time.
Do not use `==` or a loop that stops at the first difference.
